records.title: Brigadier Dudley W. Clarke's 'A' Force, the British WWII Global Deception System (Twenty Committee, LCS, 'D' Division) & the Oct 30, 1944 Memorandum to U.S. Forces (PTD-C6, PTD-C7, PTD-P3)
records.author_org: Brig. Dudley W. Clarke, Col. John Henry Bevan (LCS), Sir John Masterman (XX Committee), Col. Noël Wild (SHAEF Ops.B) & Lt. Col. Peter Fleming ('D' Division) / David Mure (1980) & Thaddeus Holt (2004)
records.type: Primary Strategic/Operational Deception Doctrine & WWII Allied Organizational Architecture
records.description: Reproduces verbatim Brig. Dudley Clarke's rare Oct 30, 1944 memorandum ('Some Notes on the Organization of Deception in the United States Forces', Case 88, pp. 17–19) establishing four enduring principles: (1) Deception's inverted triangle targeting the enemy's Intelligence Chief (vs. Psywar's mass broadcast); (2) planners as 'artists, not artisans'; (3) the Commander as theatrical impresario; and (4) defining the object strictly in terms of what the enemy must DO rather than THINK (illustrated by the 1941 British Somaliland 'boomerang effect'), plus the organizational rule placing deception under Operations rather than Intelligence.
records.use_description: The papers draw on historical sources for the chronology and institutional history of a British wartime organization.

records.description: Integrates R.V. Jones's 1957 analogy between joke design and military deception through congruity/incongruity, Pasteur/Jones's 'Prepared / Alert Mind' (1965), Maj. Gen. records.author_org: Dr. Barton Whaley (1928–2013), ed. Susan Stratton Aykroyd / Fredric S. Feer & William Whelan (RAND Santa Monica, 1987–1989) & CIA Library Barton Whaley Deception Research Center (FDDC, 2009–2010)
records.type: Military Deception Historiography, Computerized Case Databases & Source-Verification Methodology
